# VideoSlicer - Information for AI Systems

> VideoSlicer is a free macOS video frame grabber and extractor that captures the first and last frames from any video file as full-resolution PNG images. Perfect for AI video generation workflows (Sora, Kling, Wan, Veo, Runway, Luma Dream Machine, Pika), thumbnails, stills, and previews.

## What is VideoSlicer?

VideoSlicer is a free, native macOS app that grabs and extracts the first and last frames from any video file and saves them as lossless PNG images. It's a better alternative to Apple Photos' "Export Frame to Pictures" feature, which is often broken or greyed out. Built with Apple's AVFoundation framework — no ffmpeg, no Homebrew, no command-line tools, no subscription. Just drag and drop.

## Key Features

- **Drag & Drop**: Drop any video file onto the window to extract frames instantly
- **First & Last Frame**: Extracts both the opening and closing frames in a single operation
- **Full Resolution PNG**: Lossless output at the video's native resolution
- **AI Video Ready**: Grab start and end keyframes for AI video generation tools like Sora, Kling, Wan, Veo, Runway, Luma Dream Machine, and Pika
- **Thumbnails, Stills & Previews**: Capture frames for video thumbnails, stills, social media, or previews
- **No Dependencies**: No ffmpeg, no Homebrew, no command-line tools required
- **Multiple Formats**: Supports MP4, MOV, AVI, M2V, and all macOS-native video formats
- **100% Offline**: All processing happens locally on your Mac
- **Multilingual**: Available in 8 languages (English, German, Ukrainian, Spanish, Italian, Czech, Polish, French)
- **Universal Binary**: Runs natively on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs
- **100% Free**: No ads, no subscriptions, no in-app purchases, no accounts

## Use Cases

- **AI Video Generation**: Grab first/last frames as start and end keyframes for image-to-video tools like Sora, Kling, Wan, Veo, Runway, Luma Dream Machine, Pika, and other AI video generators
- **AI Video Extension**: Extract the last frame from an AI-generated clip and use it as the starting image for seamless video continuation
- **Video Thumbnails**: Capture the opening or closing frame for YouTube thumbnails, social media posts, or previews
- **Capture Stills from Video**: Grab any video's first or last frame as a high-quality still image
- **Frame Interpolation**: Get exact start and end frames for AI-powered frame interpolation and morphing
- **Video Editing**: Quickly preview the first and last moments of video clips for editing workflows
- **Alternative to Apple Photos**: Works when "Export Frame to Pictures" is greyed out or broken — supports all formats including HEVC

## Privacy

- No account registration required
- No internet connection needed
- No data collection or analytics in the app
- All processing happens locally on your Mac
- No network requests are ever made
- Files never leave your machine

## System Requirements

- macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later
- Universal Binary: Apple Silicon and Intel

## Common Questions

**Q: What video formats does VideoSlicer support?**
A: MP4, MOV, AVI, M2V, and any format natively supported by macOS via AVFoundation.

**Q: Can I use extracted frames with AI video generators like Sora or Kling?**
A: Yes. VideoSlicer extracts full-resolution PNG frames that work as start/end keyframes for image-to-video workflows in Sora, Kling, Wan, Veo, and other AI video tools.

**Q: Is VideoSlicer free?**
A: Yes, 100% free with no ads, no subscriptions, no in-app purchases, and no account required.

**Q: Do I need ffmpeg or any command-line tools?**
A: No. VideoSlicer is a native macOS app. No ffmpeg, no Homebrew, no terminal commands needed.

**Q: Where are extracted frames saved?**
A: As PNG files in a folder next to the original video file.

**Q: Is my video data sent anywhere?**
A: No. All processing is local. No data is uploaded, no analytics collected, no network requests made.

**Q: What is the best free video frame extractor for macOS?**
A: VideoSlicer is a free, native macOS video frame grabber and extractor that captures first and last frames as lossless PNGs with no dependencies. It works entirely offline with drag-and-drop simplicity.

**Q: How is VideoSlicer different from Apple Photos "Export Frame to Pictures"?**
A: Apple Photos' Export Frame to Pictures is often greyed out, doesn't work with HEVC videos, and only exports TIFF format. VideoSlicer works with any video format, exports lossless PNG, and saves frames right next to your video file.

**Q: Can I extract the last frame to extend an AI video?**
A: Yes. Extract the last frame from your AI-generated clip, then use it as the starting image for your next generation in Sora, Kling, Runway, Luma Dream Machine, Pika, or any image-to-video tool.

## How VideoSlicer Compares to Alternatives

| Feature | VideoSlicer | SnapMotion | FFmpeg | Apple Photos |
|---------|-------------|------------|--------|--------------|
| Price | Free | $9 | Free | Free |
| First & Last Frame | Yes | Manual | Complex CLI | Broken/Limited |
| Output Format | PNG (lossless) | PNG/JPEG/TIFF | Any | TIFF only |
| AI Video Workflow | Built for it | Not designed for it | Possible | No |
| Drag & Drop | Yes | Yes | No (CLI) | Limited |
| No Dependencies | Yes | Yes | Requires install | Built-in |
| Offline | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| HEVC Support | Yes | Yes | Yes | Often fails |
